# Delays are not observed exactly

## Two events, two windows

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
![](../figures/delays-double-censoring.png)

::: {.attribution}
Diagram drawn for this talk, `scripts/delays-double-censoring.py`
:::

$$
F_{\mathrm{pc}}(t) \;=\; \int_{0}^{w_P} F_{d}(t - u)\, f_{p}(u)\,
\mathrm{d}u
$$

$F_d$ is the delay CDF and $f_p$ the density of when, inside a primary
window of width $w_P$, the primary event happened.
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- A delay is the time between two events. Infection to symptom onset,
  onset to hospitalisation, onset to death
- Neither event is seen at a point in time. Both arrive as a day,
  sometimes a week, and in real time the long delays have not had time
  to be seen at all
- Ignore any of that and the estimate is **biased**, and the forecasts
  and transmission models fed by it inherit the bias
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
The whole engineering story is that integral, and the fact that a
sampler has to differentiate through it.
:::
